newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OPEC's Lukman sees firm prices in next 3-6 months.
newsitem.headline: OPEC's Lukman sees firm prices in next 3-6 months.

text.p: OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman said he expected oil prices to remain firm for the next three to six months despite the prospect of a resumption of Iraqi exports.

"We expect prices to remain reasonably firm over the next three to six months. Iraqi oil will have an effect but we believe the market is sufficiently firm to absorb this," he said, adding that he saw no market "upheavels."

Asked whether he thought current high prices would damage demand Lukman said "they will have to be a lot higher before there is any major effect on the level of demand. We would like to see prices a little bit higher."

Lukman also said that Indonesian oil minister Ida Bagus Sudjana would take Libya's place on OPEC's quota compliance committee. The committe would continue to be chaired by Iranian oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh and to also consist of Nigerian oil minister Dan Etete and OPEC Secretary-General Lukman.
In response to a question on quota monitoring, Lukman said that "a possible modification of this (the current) method is under active discussion."
